products.name: CoCounsel (Casetext)
products.note: Legal research AI; litigation support; Westlaw integration; attorney work product risk

profile_text.body:
Thomson Reuters (Nasdaq/TSX: TRI) is a publicly traded, for-profit global content and technology company. The company describes itself as delivering "technology with purpose," serving professionals in the legal, tax, accounting, trade compliance, risk, and government sectors. Its stated aim is to help professionals make faster decisions and deliver greater impact, with offerings that combine proprietary content with AI-driven tools.

The company's primary AI product is CoCounsel, which Thomson Reuters positions as a legal AI assistant built on what it calls "Fiduciary-Grade AI" principles, grounded in content from Westlaw and Practical Law. CoCounsel is described as supporting legal research, analysis, drafting, and multi-step litigation workflows. The company also offers ONESOURCE+, an AI-powered platform that connects tax, trade, legal, and risk functions, and a trade compliance AI tool focused on Harmonized System code classification for import and export. The site cites a case study in which a firm called Justly Prudent used CoCounsel and Westlaw AI and reported increasing litigation capacity by 100%. Thomson Reuters also publishes annual research, including its 2026 Future of Professionals Report and 2026 AI in Professional Services Report, the latter drawing on perspectives from more than 1,500 professionals across legal, tax, accounting, risk, fraud, and government fields.

The held facts confirm Thomson Reuters carries SEC registrant CIK 0001075124 and trades under the ticker TRI. CoCounsel is tracked separately on this site under the Casetext profile, where it is noted for Westlaw integration and attorney work product considerations. No litigation or MCP server entries are currently held for the company.
